ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.**
text: RR:155 IS ONE SENTENCE CARRYING TWO TABLES THAT NEED OPPOSITE CORRECTIONS, AND THE REWRITE WILL PICK ONE. 'The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.' Both halves are wrong in DIFFERENT directions and both fixes are already upheld. DAMAGE half: 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 IS a ceiling row - it is just labelled one rung low. §1t99s0§.as:3262 gives Light dmg x(0.5 + 0.4*lightMastery*0.1), :3265 Balanced x(1 + 0.2*balancedMastery*0.1), :3270 Heavy/Dual/Reversed flat x1.4; at mastery 10 that is 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4 exactly, and strings.json["8131"] 'Light Stance Mastery Level 10.' fixes the cap at 10. So the damage half needs MASTERY-9 -> MASTERY-10. REACH half: 300 / 200 / 100 is not a ceiling at all - the reach multipliers run the OTHER WAY (§1t99s0§.as:3094 Light x1.4 flat, :3105 Balanced x(1 + 0.02m), :3116 Heavy x(0.5 + 0.04m)), so their ceiling is 1.4 / 1.2 / 0.9, which cannot produce a 3 : 2 : 1 shape off any base. The reach triple is a MASTERY-ZERO row. So the damage half must be re-labelled UP a rung and the reach half must be re-labelled DOWN to zero, in the same sentence. A writer who applies [[cite-s27b/stance-damage-ceiling-is-mastery-10-not-mastery-9]] deletes the reach fix; a writer who applies [[combat-core/300-200-100-is-base-not-ceiling]] or either finding in my packet deletes the damage fix. The sentence must be SPLIT INTO TWO before either correction lands.
